data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Within a single evaluation, genuine reliability is distinguished from mere checklist compliance by checking for graded, uncertainty-calibrated deviations on near-threshold items: a genuine panel shows smooth error gradients near decision boundaries, whereas mere compliance produces discrete step-functions anchored to checklist thresholds.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the task's objectively verifiable outcomes are themselves binary with no near-threshold continuum, the test is inapplicable.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's intuition is also discrete (e.g., recognition-primed decision), smoothness does not distinguish panel from expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist itself encodes graded confidence rather than binary pass/fail, compliance can mimic smoothness.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Mere compliance is binary per item (pass/fail the checklist), so panel errors on near-threshold items are determined by the checklist's discrete threshold. Genuine reliability, if it reflects underlying competence, supports graded confidence and smooth error-rate gradients as item difficulty varies continuously.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
